items.sample_quote: Libraries help patrons, especially the homeless, find jobs to help get them back on their feet, and internet/wifi access is the biggest help with that. Students go to public libraries to use their Wi-Fi to study or work on building a resume for a job at age 16 because their parents can't afford internet service at home. Public libraries help their community in so many ways and having internet access is one of them.

Reducing Internet access at public schools and libraries is not the way to address the serious issue of too much screen time. Schools should review their procedures for limiting screen time particularly in the primary grades. Some states have also limited use of phones during school hours.

Please do not cut funding. There are people in our community who cannot afford computers and/or the Internet and use our library for these services. Cutting funding would hurt both seniors and school children.
This is fake medicine and is harming children

E-rate is a vital resource for our rural district. Our high population of low income students has high needs. Without e-rate funding, their access to high quality internet on campus would be affected.
Because our district relies on an 80% reimbursement rate, restricting or eliminating E-Rate would quintuple our local connectivity costs overnight.
Please keep the e-rate program to benefit schools and libraries
Defunding e-Rate would be removing access to a vital community resource for low-income citizens nationwide.

It is in the national interest to assist public libraries and schools with Internet access because this has a direct impact on creating an informed citizenry and to help our intellectually developing children. This is exactly the sort of thing govenment should be doing
We need funding to keep teaching effectively in the class.
Changes to erates will substantially change our budget and funding and will impact services to students and to the community
The E-Rate program is an important source of funding to Ashland City Schools.
Reliable internet is imperative to education today!

It is because of the E-Rate program that the schools I attended, and the few public libraries I visited during my youth, were able to provide me with the ability to access the internet and gave me the potential to learn as much as I could. Therefore, I believe screen-time expectations should remain strictly a local issue
Having an affordable high-quality internet access is meaningful to library patrons who rely on the library for internet access, and allows the library to provide excellent service to patrons.

Defunding or scaling back this service would be a great disservice and be an active move to try to limit the information and connectivity of lower income individuals and families, while putting stress and pressure on already low funded schools and libraries to continue offering equal or relatively similar services without this aid.
